top_violation_types.title: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited (26 TAC §746.1201(4))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: This standard was found deficient as part of a DFPS Investigation.

top_violation_types.title: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk (26 TAC §746.307(b)(4))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The operation did not notify parent in a timely manner of a situation involving their child.

top_violation_types.title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))
HRC42.052(d) - Illegal Operation - Not Registered (26 TAC §HRC42.052(d) - Illegal Operation - Not R)
top_violation_types.typical_finding: There were 5 unrelated children found in care at the time of inspection.

top_violation_types.title: Annual Sanitation Inspection (26 TAC §746.3401(a))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The operation did not have a current health inspection.

top_violation_types.title: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days (26 TAC §746.2421(b))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: Two infants did not have current infant feeding schedules.

top_violation_types.title: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.305(a)(6))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: A report was not made to Child Care Regulation for an incident that potentially posed a risk to children.

top_violation_types.title: Medication Authorization Expires on First Anniversary (26 TAC §746.3803(b))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: CCR observed that a child with a food allergy had an expired EpiPen.
